Packing Guide

Understanding CaPackyBara Parameters

1. Data Input

Two formats are accepted. Both UTF-8 and UTF-16 files load without fuss.

  • Museum TSV export: Columns are Object short summary · Nomenclature Classification Category · Dimensions LWH comma separate · Image Ref - Relative path.
  • Plain CSV: Columns are name, type, length_mm, width_mm, height_mm.
  • Image refs: Images sit in a folder named after your import file, extension included, with _Media on the end. Each ref is read as a path inside it. So frog.txt looks in frog.txt_Media/ and foo.tsv looks in foo.tsv_Media/. Two ways to supply it: drop the folder next to this HTML file (rename the import file and the folder has to follow), or use Images Folder (local) to pick any folder on your machine — matched by relative path first, then file name. Picked images stay in your browser and are never uploaded.
  • Missing dimensions: Any object without a length or width takes the assumed size set under Data Input (50 mm by default).

2. Internal Item Padding

This is the protective buffer around each object before it goes into a tray. Choose one of two strategies.

Proportional Strategy Padding is a percentage of the object's dimensions, held between Min Pad and Max Pad. Larger objects get more room, and nothing gets an unreasonable amount.
Flat Strategy The same fixed millimetre value goes on every side, whatever the size of the object. Simple and predictable.
  • Padded L × W: The two longest dimensions, laid flat, plus (2 × Side Padding).
  • Padded H: The shortest dimension, standing vertically, plus Depth Pad and Lid Clearance.
  • Depth Pad: Extra foam or base material under the object.
  • Lid Clearance: Headspace above the object so the lid closes without touching it.

3. Tray Configuration

Objects are packed into standard trays first. The trays are the modular units that stack inside the crates.

  • Standard Tray Depths: Set in fixed increments, for example 50 and 100 mm. Each padded height rounds up to the next valid depth.
  • Tray Footprints: The L × W base sizes on offer. The packer picks the smallest footprint that fits the grouped objects.
  • Grouping: Objects are batched either by Type and Depth, or by Depth alone, before packing.

4. External Crate Allowances

These are the structural dimensions added outside the tray footprint to arrive at the final crate size.

Final Crate Width = Tray Width + (2 × Side Walls)
Final Crate Length = Tray Length + (2 × Side Walls)
Final Crate Height = Base Board + Top Clearance + Σ(Tray Depths + Interlayers)
  • Side Walls: Wall thickness on all four vertical sides.
  • Base Board: Thickness of the bottom pallet or base structure.
  • Top Clearance: Space or lid thickness at the top of the crate.
  • Interlayer: Divider thickness between trays stacked in the same crate.

5. Consolidation & Limits

  • Min Utilization: The fill percentage a tray must reach before the system tries merging it with another partly filled tray.
  • Cross-type Fill: When on, different object types may share a tray during consolidation.
  • Max Crate Dimensions: Hard physical limits. A stack that exceeds them splits into multiple crates. Set to 0 for no limit, though your loading dock may disagree.
  • Oversized Handling: Anything that fits no standard tray footprint gets its own custom crate.
